## claude.ai Era Context
Era Context is an MCP-first, agent-native personal finance management platform. Every capability is exposed via MCP tools, and professional users can also access the same data via REST API. The platform provides both read and write access to the user's finances across connected third-party accounts. Capabilities are organized into plan tiers: See, Organize, Automate, and Optimize.

## Tool domains

**Knowledge & Memory** — Centralized memory shared across all connected agents and the user's dashboard. Era Context may have pending onboarding or follow-up questions queued for the agent to ask — some unlock capabilities, others can be snoozed. Use these tools to surface questions, record answers, and capture facts, preferences, goals, or aspirations from natural conversation. Ambient observations (e.g. lifestyle preferences, financial goals, casual remarks) improve personalization over time. Facts can carry expiry dates for automatic re-verification. User data is never shared with third parties and is anonymized during any LLM inference conducted by Era Context.

**Accounts & Transactions** — Query balances, search and categorize transactions, manage tags across the user's connected accounts at third-party institutions.

**Insights & Analysis** — Spending breakdowns, cash flow, period comparisons, forecasting, and daily summaries.

**Automation & Rules** — User-defined rules for transaction cleanup, filtering, and categorization that execute automatically.

**Billing** — Current plan details and upgrade options. Capabilities vary by tier.

Upcoming: automated money movement between connected accounts; shared household views for group finance management.

## Session lifecycle

knowledge__get_financial_context_and_overview loads the user's profile, financial snapshot, known facts, goals, and personalization state in a single call. Its response includes a `personalization.guidance_quality` field: when not 'ready', the response contains pending onboarding questions whose answers improve guidance accuracy. ## claude.ai freddy Oura MCP
freddy is the user's personal health-data server: sleep, workouts, recovery, HRV, glucose and body metrics from their connected sources (wearables, rings, CGMs, training platforms, gym logs, sensors).

How to query: call list_metrics once per conversation to discover the exact metric names this user has — names are provider-specific (e.g. wellness_sleepSecs, blood_glucose_avg), so never guess generic English names. Then call query_metrics with those names; the default window is the last 7 days.

Account limits: This account can query the last 7 days of synced data. It queries one connected source at a time (currently showing Oura); other connected sources keep syncing in the background but are not queryable. Responses cap at 500 rows (fewer with include_raw); a truncated response states the date range it covered and how to continue.

Long time ranges: pass `start` and `end` (YYYY-MM-DD) — required for windows beyond 1 year. For multi-month or multi-year questions pass granularity: "week" or "month" to get avg/min/max buckets that fit years of data in one response; prefer daily-summary metrics (the *_avg / *_min / *_max variants shown by list_metrics) over per-reading metrics, and when a response reports truncation, follow its continuation hint to page backwards through the range.

Raw detail (per-set workouts, sleep-stage hypnograms, per-second workout samples, CGM streams) is available via query_metrics with include_raw — list_metrics flags which metrics carry it. Keep raw windows narrow.

Freshness: sources sync automatically (webhooks plus a daily pull). sync_source forces a refresh; new data lands asynchronously, so re-query after about 30-60 seconds. If a response notes a sync in progress, do not conclude data is missing.

Connectable sources include Polar, Oura, Withings, Intervals.icu, Suunto, Concept2, Wahoo, Ultrahuman, Hevy, Airthings, WHOOP, Garmin Connect, Apple Health, Health Connect. Use connect_source to add one; some sources finish connecting on the freddy dashboard or phone app instead of from th… [truncated]

## claude.ai Intuit Credit Karma
Credit Karma helps you understand your credit health. Get a breakdown of the key factors affecting your credit score — including payment history, credit utilization, credit age, credit mix, new credit inquiries, and total accounts — and see how you're rated on each to help you take action toward improving your credit.

## claude.ai Monarch MCP
Monarch Money MCP Server.

Access to the authenticated user's Monarch Money data, scoped to their household.
Authenticate via OAuth 2.1 PKCE — connect this server in your MCP client to start
the flow.

The read tools return stable IDs for the entities they list (categories, tags,
merchants, business entities, rules, household members, transactions). The write
tools take those IDs only — there is no name-based matching on writes.

Workflow: use a read tool to find an entity and its ID (e.g. GetMerchants(search=...),
GetCategories, GetHouseholdMembers), then pass the ID to the write tool. To reference
a merchant that does not exist yet, create it with CreateMerchant and use the returned
merchant_id.

Balance history for a manual account (one that does not sync from an institution) can be
uploaded with UpdateAccountBalanceHistory using the account id from GetAccounts.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

That confirms it. `Check In / Submit` is the **pre-rename name** — it was renamed to `Submit To FM/EC` in commit `cc48e4e` via migration `0005_rename_fm_submit_task.sql`, which ran successfully against this workspace's dev database (that's your "3 tasks locally", correctly named).

**Root cause:** per `CLAUDE.md`, the API server only auto-runs DB migrations "if the `shows` table does not yet exist — otherwise it skips to avoid re-applying already-applied migrations." Your production database already had a `shows` table when `0005` was added, so on every subsequent deploy the server skipped *all* migrations, including `0005`. The old `Check In / Submit` row was never renamed there — and it looks like `Submit To FM/EC` also exists online (likely added separately, possibly manually), so you're left with **both** the old and new names as separate rows: 4 total instead of 3.

That also explains the "doesn't categorize properly" symptom: `dashboard.ts`/`shows.ts` and the key-task star logic in `task-list.tsx` specifically match on the name `"Submit To FM/EC"` — so the leftover `Check In / Submit` preset doesn't get the star icon, doesn't drive the FM "Submitted" chip, and behaves like an ordinary (deletable/editable) task instead of the key task it's supposed to be.

**Fix — two options:**

1. **Simplest (no DB access needed):** In the deployed app, go to **Settings**, find `Check In / Submit` under Fire Marshal, and delete it with the trash icon. Deleting a *preset* only removes the template — it won't touch any tasks already created on existing shows from that preset.
2. **Proper fix for the underlying drift:** manually run `pnpm --filter @workspace/db run migrate` against production's `DATABASE_URL` so `0005` (and any future migrations) actually get applied there, instead of relying on the "skip if `shows` exists" auto-migrate.
